# Revised essays 4–5 and a broader candidate pool

22 October 2026. Prepared in response to the user's request for stronger philosophical contributions, near-limit drafts, at least 100 further ideas, and progressive assessment emphasizing importance and originality. Claude's GitHub reports and issue comments informed both revisions.

## Read the essays

| Essay | Markdown | PDF | Words excluding references |
|---|---|---|---:|
| 4 — What Counts as the Same Evidence? | [Source](essays/04-evidence-and-description.md) | [PDF](essays/04-evidence-and-description.pdf) | 5,980 |
| 5 — Can Regret Minimization Determine What to Believe? | [Source](essays/05-regret-and-belief.md) | [PDF](essays/05-regret-and-belief.pdf) | 5,976 |

Counts use the repository's strict whitespace-token method after Markdown stripping, including titles, abstracts, headings, tables, and displayed mathematics. They exclude the bibliography. These drafts aim just below the 6,000-word ceiling; an organizer's word-processing convention may differ. No final submission or competition-compliance certification is implied.

Essay 4 replaces a broad representation-neutrality objection with an account of when a fixed-space accuracy justification can be transported. It connects weighted accuracy to CAR explicitly, gives an exact criterion for a specified compression, and shows why merely preserving truth is insufficient.

Essay 5 replaces an overbroad objection to robust updating with a distinction between policy optimality and justified belief. It proves a general binary proper-loss equalizer, characterizes the known boosting score by prior preservation, and accepts the least-favorable Bayesian representation instead of portraying regret as weight-free.

See the [response to Claude](audit/response-to-claude.md), [validation and provenance record](audit/validation.md), and [numerical check results](audit/check-results.json). The proofs are in the essays. The checks are small reproducible spot checks, not a new formal pipeline.

The eight priorities are C013 (revocation and independent monitoring), C052 (responsibility-preserving causal abstraction), C004 (preserving future defeasibility), C111 (successors' authority over inherited projects), C063 (translation and disputability), C045 (explaining obligations after memory loss), C085 (authority to close and reopen inquiry), and C021 (standing to contest institutional objectives). This is a research queue, not eight certified discoveries.

These are successive judgments by one assistant, not an independent panel. Targeted source checks already demoted attractive but crowded proposals, including generic evidential-damage liability, exit versus voice, shared model blind spots, and ongoing consent. Full argument validity remains for later rounds, as requested; an already identified prior-art collision is not hidden until then.

## Suggested next round for Claude

The current branch's STATUS records an ambitious hard-problems track. This pool can supply attack cards and alternatives for it; it does not replace that track or its existing work.

Start with C013, C052, C004, and C111, representing distinct questions. For each, read the nearest primary texts in full and write a one-page argument with a concrete counterexample to the closest account. Promote only proposals whose significance survives that comparison. Keep C063 and C045 as alternatives; compare C085 against C004 before developing both. C021 carries a particularly high contestability-literature overlap risk.

Do not select merely for easy formalization or for a proof that can be put in code. An illuminating distinction or substantive normative argument may be the strongest essay. Conversely, a correct new formula can remain philosophically minor. The next round should make that assessment explicit before commissioning another long draft.

The copies here are a self-contained revision package. Existing draft files, blind review bundles, and other agents' work remain available for comparison. No issue replies or messages to outside reviewers were sent.
